greeting.speaker: Rook the Watchman
text: Nobody crosses the causeway at this hour without a reason. Let's hear yours.
Stop there. Hands where the torch can find them, and talk.
Four hours I've had of nothing but wind, and now you. Make it worth the walk over.

options.text: We fought whatever's been coming out of the gate. Ask anyone on the road.
Something for the cold, and no questions from us.
Try to stop us and find out.

again.speaker: Rook the Watchman
text: It's you. Go up — I'll not do the whole speech twice in one season.
Same causeway, same wind. You're the only thing that changes out here.
They've stopped asking me who you are. That's either good for you or very bad.

known.speaker: Rook the Watchman
known.text: ...I know that name. Go up. Don't make me regret saying so.

not_known.speaker: Rook the Watchman
not_known.text: Then you wait out here with everyone else who is expected.

the_gate.speaker: Rook the Watchman
the_gate.text: Everyone on the road says that. The difference is you still have the mud on you. Go up.

backed_down.speaker: Rook the Watchman
backed_down.text: Steady. Steady. I've a wife inside that wall and I'd like to see her again — go up.

the_watch.speaker: Rook the Watchman
the_watch.text: The castellan set it, back when there were enough of us to take turns. Now it's set itself, and I'm what's left standing in it.

the_coin.speaker: Rook the Watchman
the_coin.text: That's not a bribe, that's a kindness, and I'll take it as the second. Go up.

since_you_left.speaker: Rook the Watchman
text: Carts going the wrong way. Full ones, leaving. Nobody comes back for a full cart.
Something walked the causeway at third watch and didn't ring the boards. I've said nothing until now.
Nothing. Which used to be the good answer.

the_wife.speaker: Rook the Watchman
the_wife.text: Furious. She's counted the hours I've stood out here and put a number on it, and the number is unkind. Ask me again in spring.
